summary: Local-first two-plane architecture for the GoneOps MVP: a React dashboard and layered Express control plane manage one generated Docker Compose sandbox per environment, with PostgreSQL as the ownership, metadata, lifecycle, and recovery authority. The remaining MVP fixes preserve those boundaries by making shared-network DNS names sandbox-unique and keeping frontend environment state and pipeline reads environment-scoped.
components: Root Docker Compose control plane with nginx, React/Vite/TailwindCSS frontend, Express backend, PostgreSQL, Redis, and RabbitMQ on goneops_net
React Router dashboard shell and twelve API-backed pages with shared project and environment selection
Layered Express HTTP controllers, application services, PostgreSQL repositories, and injectable filesystem, Docker, HTTP proxy, log, and terminal adapters
PostgreSQL schema for projects, environments, services, deployments, environment-scoped pipeline runs and steps, secrets, and transactional sandbox port reservations
Atomic template-based sandbox generator producing Express source, Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, environment files, and README.md in an owned working directory
Sandbox Compose networking with resource-prefix aliases for web, db, redis, and mq on the shared external goneops_net
Docker Compose lifecycle, logs, bounded sandbox HTTP proxy, and container-only WebSocket terminal transport with an explicit backend-client/host-daemon filesystem boundary
Six-step persisted simulated CI/CD pipeline with pollable asynchronous execution and deployment metadata
Startup operation reconciler and idempotent lifecycle/pipeline executors for persisted transitional states
nginx same-origin API and WebSocket proxy with SPA fallback
ProjectContext selection reconciler that validates persisted project and environment IDs against the latest project payload
Environment-scoped pipeline client contract that forwards environment_id on history reads as well as pipeline runs
constraints: The required 14 REST endpoint paths and methods remain stable; supporting endpoints are additive and environment-scoped.
Routes cannot directly access SQL, filesystem APIs, child processes, Docker, or raw sandbox HTTP.
Long-running lifecycle and pipeline operations return HTTP 202 after persisting an owned, pollable transitional state; in-memory jobs and mutexes are never authoritative.
Environment lifecycle transitions use PostgreSQL compare-and-set updates; pipeline runs allow at most one active run per environment.
Sandbox generation reserves ports transactionally, renders into a temporary directory, atomically replaces files, and rolls back metadata and filesystem state on failure.
Every environment-scoped operation verifies project ownership; file reads also require an allowlist, realpath confinement, and bounded file size.
Docker commands use fixed executable argument arrays, bounded timeouts, and output limits; request data is never interpolated into a shell.

Generated Compose files cannot use backend-container-local host bind paths; working_dir is a control-plane CLI and file-browser path, while sandbox persistence uses images, named volumes, and goneops_net.

Every generated service must publish a resource-prefix network alias on goneops_net; web must address db, redis, and mq through those unique aliases rather than shared Compose service names, which are reserved for same-project declarations such as depends_on.
The checked-in sandbox Compose template and the generator's inline fallback must emit equivalent network aliases and dependency host values until the inline fallback is removed.
Persisted transitional lifecycle and pipeline states must be idempotently reconciled after backend restart without duplicate steps, deployments, services, secrets, or ports.
Terminal access is localhost-only and restricted to the owned running sandbox web container, never the backend container or host shell.
Secrets are localhost-only plaintext for the MVP, masked by default, excluded from logs, and documented as not production-safe.
Frontend runtime data must come from real backend APIs; unsupported services and controls are disabled instead of mocked.

Persisted selectedEnvironmentId is valid only when it belongs to selectedProject; after project data loads or refreshes, stale selections repair to that project's first environment or clear when none exists, updating localStorage in the same transition.
Pipeline history requests from the Pipelines page require both selectedProjectId and selectedEnvironmentId and send environment_id so project-level history cannot leak across environment views.
The iframe preview is best-effort; server-side Test API is the reliable integration path.
Implementation is conformant only after Compose rendering checks, focused environment-selection and pipeline request tests, the frontend build, and all seven Playwright E2E specs pass.
